Fixed in 09e25f8. The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

Fixed and confirmed green. CI run 33896102710 on b24ce5f is the repository's first successful run: Node 22.12 quality gate, Node 24 quality gate, and the installer/package jobs on ubuntu and macOS all pass. Fixes: the renderer accepts MCP_BPMN_BROWSER_ARGS and adds --no-sandbox under uid 0, the workflow sets that flag, and the e2e drain test now throws the real tool result plus server stderr instead of a bare marker timeout. Two regressions found and fixed while verifying: regenerating the lockfiles from scratch on Linux dropped 24 @esbuild platform binaries and fsevents, which npm 11 on Node 24 rejects; and the dependency overrides pushed npm audit onto the retiring quick-audit endpoint, which returned 'Invalid package tree'. Both resolved by advancing fast-uri and qs within their existing declared ranges. Branch protection on the check job remains a repository setting the maintainer must enable.

runRender now takes a bounded FIFO semaphore slot instead of throwing: overlapping exports queue, and only a wait list longer than maxQueuedRenders (default 32) is rejected. close() rejects waiters. Pinned by tests/integration/svg-export.test.ts (queueing, queue-limit, close-while-queued).

save_png gained scale (1-4, config MAX_PNG_SCALE) mapped to Puppeteer deviceScaleFactor, and the result now reports width, height, scale and downscaled. Large diagrams still downscale but say so in the message. Pinned by svg-export.test.ts and artifact-persistence.test.ts.

Already fixed earlier in this release cycle: BpmnSvgRenderer caches this.browser and getBrowser() reuses it across renders, relaunching only after a disconnect. Pinned by svg-export.test.ts 'reuses one browser without leaking render pages until shutdown', which asserts launchBrowser is called once for two exports.

applyAutoLayout now parses the adapter result, applies the collaboration policy and any transposition, then compares a geometry signature (element/lane bounds, connection waypoints, shape isHorizontal) against the live document. An identical layout is not committed: no revision bump, no file write, and the tool returns changed:false with a message saying so. Pinned by tests/unit/core/LayoutOrientation.test.ts.

auto_layout gained the direction option named as the primary fix: left-to-right (default) and top-to-bottom, implemented as the transposition + re-docking the issue specified (src/core/layout/LayoutOrientation.ts). Pools become vertical bands with isHorizontal false, containers reflect whole so contents stay inside, ordinary shapes keep their proportions, and boundary events are re-attached. MermaidConverter now lays TD/TB/BT out downward and warns that BT/RL read back to front; capabilities.md and README corrected. spacing, scopeId and pinnedElementIds are not feasible against bpmn-auto-layout's option-free API and are tracked in mcp-bpmn-9sv.16.

Already fixed earlier in this release cycle: ANCHORED_FILE_WORKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS is 5s (src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts:54), not 100ms, so a worker survives ordinary inter-request gaps. Pinned by tests/unit/utils/SafeFilePath.test.ts 'reuses its anchored worker across ordinary request gaps', which asserts the child pid is unchanged across a 250ms gap. Left the timeout a constant rather than a ResourceLimits field: no caller has a reason to tune it and the issue offered that as an alternative, not a requirement.

connect now raises missingEndpointError(context, side, elementId), which names whether the source or the target is missing, gives the id, and says when the id exists but is not a flow node. Pinned in tests/integration/handlers.test.ts.

The mandatory-revision superRefine on update_connection was removed from tools.ts and the matching guard from SimpleBpmnEngine.updateConnection. A label change is now a single call; expectedRevision and expectedSemanticRevision remain available for callers that want the optimistic guard.

save_as gained the overwrite parameter its error message already advertised. The handler threads it through commitMutation's replaceTarget, reports previousFilename and removedPreviousFile, and a generated placeholder filename is replaced rather than left orphaned.

connect's tool description now states that endpoints in one process get a SequenceFlow and endpoints in different participants of a collaboration get a MessageFlow, and that condition/isDefault are sequence-flow only. README's connect section, the tool-area table, and the Known Limitations entry were corrected to match; the limitation is now the real one, that the type is inferred and cannot be requested.

update_element accepts text and textFormat in properties; BpmnDocument writes bpmn:TextAnnotation/text and defaults textFormat to text/plain on both sides of the comparison so a round trip no longer reports a spurious semantic difference.

documentation is now a first-class field on add_event, add_activity, add_gateway, connect and update_element; BpmnDocument.applyDocumentation writes bpmn:Documentation and import reads it back, and assertElementProperties accepts it as a supported property.
updateConnection now rejects a label on a bpmn:Association instead of reporting success and dropping it on save. The assertion that encoded the old behaviour was updated deliberately.

safeImportError was inverted: structural messages are forwarded verbatim and the generic 'malformed or invalid input' text is used only for a genuine BpmnXmlParseError, which BpmnDocument now throws from the XML-parse boundary.

assertElementProperties exempts start events whose containing scope has triggeredByEvent true, so a rename inside an imported event subprocess succeeds. triggeredByEvent is captured on import, written back on serialize, and listed as a supported property.

Moddle's materialized schema defaults (waitForCompletion, cancelActivity, textFormat, calledElementBinding) are no longer captured as authored payload, and waitForCompletion is deleted rather than assigned undefined so the serializer cannot emit the literal string 'undefined'.

The compensation-boundary rule now fires only when cancelActivity is explicitly written in the source XML, detected by elementIdsDeclaringAttribute. The pinned false positive on the Camunda C7 fixture was removed.
registerConnectionOnEndpoints maintains bpmn:incoming and bpmn:outgoing for flows added to imported documents whenever either endpoint already uses that convention.

Added EVENT_BASED_GATEWAY_TARGET_DEFINITIONS with isEventBasedGatewayTarget in the engine and validateEventBasedGatewayTarget in the validator, so an illegal target is rejected by connect and reported by validate.

The validator gained validateFlowCondition and validateDefaultFlows, matching the rules the engine already enforced on its own mutations. validateDefaultFlows also inspects node.$attrs.default, which is where moddle puts the attribute on imported documents.

SafeFilePath's compare-and-write lock now carries an owner record (uuid, pid, host, time). A lock whose pid is dead on this host, or older than 30s, is reclaimed through an O_EXCL claim keyed to the exact holder record, and assertLockHeld runs immediately before the destructive rename so a writer that lost its lock can never publish. The busy error names the lock directory. Pinned by five cases in tests/unit/utils/SafeFilePath.test.ts.

Persistence failures now name the file, the workspace and the cause (FileManager.describeStorageFailure), built from errno symbols only so no path or content leaks through Node's message. The pinned root is revalidated before every operation and re-pinned only when the configured path is not a symlink, so a recreated workspace no longer needs a restart. Read errors deliberately stay path-free.

The configured workspace, not the launch cwd, is now the startup boundary for both repository_config and environment sources, and resolveSelection no longer creates directories unless the caller passes create:true. select_workspace's description and schema now say the directory must already exist, and the boundary error is classified as file_not_found with a recovery hint. New tests/security/workspace-containment.test.ts pins both halves; three assertions that encoded the old behaviour were updated deliberately.

ConnectionRouter now charges FOREIGN_INTERIOR_COST_PER_UNIT for every unit a route runs inside a participant that does not own the connection, so a message flow leaves its pool instead of crossing a foreign one. Folded into the route total rather than adding a scoring field, following the dockSidePenalty precedent. Pinned by tests/unit/layout/ConnectionRouter.test.ts.

LayoutEngine.ts and AutoLayout.ts were already deleted; what remained was the leftover jest.config.js coverage ignore for a file that no longer exists and two docs claiming a second layout path. Both removed, and IMPLEMENTATION.md and engine-contract.md now record that there is one layout path.

Deleted the genuinely unreachable parts: both layout barrels, bpmnDocumentToLayoutModel, processContextToLayoutModel and mermaidAstToLayoutModel. MermaidAstLayoutAdapter.toLayoutModel and validateLayoutModel turned out to be production-reachable through SimpleBpmnGenerator, so the issue's premise held only in part. BpmnDocumentLayoutAdapter still hangs off the caller-less getLayoutModel/applyLayoutModel pair; tracked separately rather than removed here.

Removed 158 lines of dead PROPERTY_PAYLOAD_LIMITS, copySafeProperties and PropertyPayloadError from tools.ts along with the SafeJsonObject/SafeJsonValue imports they alone used. The limits they described were never enforced, so nothing shipping changed.

Every Mermaid shape now tries a quoted body first, so quotes are delimiters and ], |, &, --> and markdown backticks inside them are kept as the label. Quoted labels decode #quot;/#35; entity codes; unquoted text stays verbatim. Subgraph titles use the same decoder. The assertion that expected the quotes to survive was updated deliberately.

The shape table matches the longest delimiter first and rejects nine valid-but-unsupported Mermaid shapes plus the Mermaid 11 @{...} form with a new UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE error naming the supported replacement, instead of silently approximating them as a Task with delimiter garbage in the name.

parseConnector now accepts -->, --->, ---, ==>, ===, -.-> and -.- with labels written inline or between pipes, expands & endpoint lists as a cartesian product, converts arrowless and thick links as directed sequence flows with a dropped-styling warning, and rejects ~~~, <-->, <==>, --o and --x with UNSUPPORTED_CONNECTOR.

subgraph now accepts id[Title], id["Title"], "Title" and bare Title, deriving a unique ID from a title that has none. A malformed declaration pushes a placeholder so its end is not reported again: one error per problem instead of a cascade.

A non-decision node with two or more outgoing sequence flows now raises IMPLICIT_PARALLEL_SPLIT at that node's own line and column. Cross-subgraph message flows are excluded and the conversion output is unchanged, so the warning informs without changing behaviour.

Fixed with mcp-bpmn-9sv.15: MermaidConverter now maps TD/TB/BT onto the new top-to-bottom layout orientation and LR/RL onto left-to-right, transposing the laid-out document rather than ignoring the declaration. BT and RL read back to front, which BPMN cannot express, so they are laid out forwards and reported in the conversion warnings. capabilities.md and the README state the actual mapping. Pinned by tests/unit/core/LayoutOrientation.test.ts.

engine-contract.md's gap list became a Resolved gaps section naming the assertion that covers each of the six, and the coverage matrix grew from 22 rows to all 40 tools in tools/list order with a verified Coverage column. The dependency audit table now lists all nine production deps and the disposition decision is past tense.

README gained a Diagram filenames section written from the code: the placeholder is mcp-bpmn-v1_<base64url([id,name,uuid])>.bpmn, the {id}_{name}_{uuid} form is only the over-200-byte fallback, and save_as deletes a placeholder but never a chosen name. The optional filename arguments on new_bpmn, new_from_mermaid and open_mermaid_file are documented in each tool's section.

Removed the false LayoutEngine claim from IMPLEMENTATION.md, replaced the '~/mcp-bpmn' default with the real three-step workspace resolution in IMPLEMENTATION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, and rebuilt the README env table from src/config with all 16 variables, their effect and default. Project structure and Key Components now match the tree on disk.

README's tarball figures were remeasured with npm pack --dry-run --json: 357,920 B packed, 2,079,332 B unpacked, 141 files, with the composition breakdown that explains the size. The stale 195 kB / 1,104,270 B numbers are gone.

README gained a Browser download section: the measured 652 MB Puppeteer cache, PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD and PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH, and the fact that make install never downloads so it relies on the shared cache, a system Chrome, or the env var. Cross-referenced from CONTRIBUTING.md.

scripts/package-smoke.mjs now byte-compares package-lock.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json and fails with the safe repair (npm install, never delete-and-reinstall). CONTRIBUTING.md documents why there are two lockfiles and the two regressions that came from regenerating them the wrong way.

Added the test:ralph script and appended it to test:all, so ralph-loop/tests/loop_test.sh runs in CI. Added a jq/perl/git prerequisite guard so a missing tool fails clearly. The suite is hermetic: it builds temp fixtures with fake bd, codex and claude on PATH.

Dropped the bpmn-auto-layout-alpha dev alias; the layout-candidate tests now import the production bpmn-auto-layout at the same version. The three dev-only comparison candidates sit behind MCP_BPMN_LAYOUT_CANDIDATES=1, which test:all sets, so npm test went from 9.5s and 73 subprocesses to 3.5s and 19 while CI still runs the full matrix. Both lockfiles were regenerated in place with npm install --package-lock-only and npm ci verified clean.
